1. (Currently Amended) A cell comprising: a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide from a bacterial species distinct from the bacterial species of the host cell.

2. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment is self-assembled in vivo.

3. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment further comprises at least one targeted enzyme that catalyzes a reaction distinct from propanediol utilization.

4. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 wherein the non-native compartment comprises a plurality of different targeted enzymes with distinct substrate specificities.

5. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 4 wherein the at least one targeted enzyme comprises a compartment-specific targeting signal sequence.

8. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the proteinaceous shell comprises a plurality of different BMC polypeptides from distinct bacterial sources.

12. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: introducing into a host cell a polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and at least one enzymatic activity distinct from that produced by Parsons et al., thereby producing a transformed cell; and growing the transformed cell under conditions effective for the transformed cell to express the polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and produce a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising the at least one BMC polypeptide.

21. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: providing a cell comprising a non-native compartment comprising: a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide from a distinct bacterial species, and at least one enzyme that catalyzes conversion of a substrate to a product that is different from propionate; and growing the cell under conditions effective for the at least one enzyme to catalyze conversion of the substrate to a product.
